problem_summary.summary: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring in which no character appears more than once.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a string s containing English letters, digits, symbols, and spaces. Return an integer length; the empty string has answer 0.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces

brute_force.explanation: For each start position, extend a fresh set of seen characters until the next character repeats, tracking the longest valid span.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every substring has a start position considered by the outer loop. For that start, the scan visits all consecutive extensions up to (but not including) the first repeated character; no longer extension from that start can be valid.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) expected — each start may scan most of the remaining characters, with expected constant-time set operations.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(min(n, alphabet size)) auxiliary — the set contains distinct characters from one active scan.

optimized.explanation: Maintain a window with unique characters and a map of each character's most recent index. On a repeat inside the window, jump the left boundary past its previous occurrence.
optimized.correctness_idea: The left boundary never moves backward. After processing each right endpoint, any repeated character in the window has been excluded by moving left beyond its earlier occurrence, so the current window is unique. Every valid substring ending at that right endpoint is no longer than the maintained window.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) expected — each character is processed once with expected constant-time map operations.
optimized.space_complexity: O(min(n, alphabet size)) auxiliary — the map holds last positions for distinct characters seen.
